description: Add a measurement history. A history is a floating point variable that can be sampled and stored during a model run, allowing tracking of measurement quantities over time. The history records values such as porosity, coordination number, stress, strain rate, position, or radius from a specified measurement object as the simulation progresses. Live 9.7: the quantity slot was fully enumerated (Batch P1); an object selector (id <i> or position <v>) is REQUIRED after the quantity - omitting it fails with 'No object for history specified'.

6.0: Live 6.00 first-slot enumeration; an object selector is required after the quantity.
7.0: Live 7.0 first-slot enumeration; an object selector is required after the quantity (same grammar as 9.x).
9.0: Live 9.7 first-slot enumeration; an object selector is required after the quantity. The former official-page spellings (magnitude/index/log/position/vector/zz/rotation) are rejected per-keyword on live 9.7.

notes: Python SDK can access history data after recording
History system is PFC-wide, not specific to measurements
Command interface simplest for setting up measurement histories
Python useful for programmatic history data processing

examples.description: Track porosity of measurement 1 over time (auto-assign history ID). Use case: Monitor void fraction evolution during compaction.
Create history with ID 10 to track coordination number of measurement 1. Use case: Explicit history ID for organization.
Track vertical stress (zz-component) in measurement 1. Use case: Monitor vertical stress during loading.
Track xx-component of strain rate in measurement 2. Use case: Monitor deformation rate during shearing.

examples.command:
measure create id 1 radius 5.0
measure history porosity id 1
measure history coordination id 1
measure history stress-zz id 1
model cycle 10000
examples.description: Create measurement, setup multiple histories, run simulation. Use case: Complete workflow to track porosity, coordination, and stress during simulation.

examples.description: Track x and y coordinates of measurement center. Use case: Monitor if measurement region is moving (e.g., tracking a moving particle cluster).
